title: Rotational Partition Functions of Polyatomic Molecules Depend on the Sphar of the Molecule
lead: A polyatomic molecule rotates about three principal axes, and how its three moments of inertia compare sorts it into a spherical, symmetric or asymmetric top. Each kind of top has its own rotational partition function.
notes: Adapted from B. L. Tembe's lecture notes (IIT Bombay, www.chem.iitb.ac.in/~bltembe/pdfs/ch_3.pdf), shared under the book's CC BY-NC-SA 4.0; the lone "and:" between the closing energy and heat capacity is left out where the derivation takes their place.
exercise_notes: The book prints no exercises for this section; the one here is new and AI-written, its answer checked by computation, with its Bloom level and concept tags chosen by AI.

exercises.source_id: Calculate the rotational partition function at 300 K.
exercises.prompt: The rotational partition function of $\mathrm{NO_2}$ is 2238 at 300 K. Without the rotational temperatures, find it at 600 K.

answer.hint: In Equation 18.8.3 only $\kT^3$ changes with temperature.
answer.solution: By Equation 18.8.3, $\kqrot = (\sqrt{\pi}/\sigma)\sqrt{\kT^3/\kThetaA\kThetaB\kThetaC}$, so $\kqrot$ grows as $\kT^{3/2}$ and everything else cancels in the ratio: $\kqrot(600\ \text{K}) = 2238 \times (600/300)^{3/2} = 2238 \times 2.828 = 6330$. A linear molecule's $\kqrot$ grows only as $\kT$, since it has two rotational degrees of freedom to the nonlinear molecule's three.

footnotes.html: Each of the sums is zero: $\sum_i m_ix_i = \sum_i m_iy_i = \sum_i m_iz_i = 0$.
With the inertia products defined as these sums, the second equation is $-\alpha I_{xy} + \beta(I_{yy} - \eta) - \gamma I_{yz} = 0$.
The first rotational temperature is 11.5 K, the value the solution uses.
